proof_summary: Take the counterexample \(n=p=2\): at argument \(4\), the numerator and denominator products both equal \(96\), so \(a(4)=1\) and hence \(\operatorname{ord}_2(a(4))=0\). On the proposed right-hand side only the \(i=0\) term is nonzero, giving \(\lfloor 2/2\rfloor=1\), so the two sides disagree.
